Desk-study packs: what someone doing a site assessment would want on hand before going to site. They follow the questions a geotechnical desk study asks: what is underground, where the water is, what could move, what might be contaminated, what is buried, and how to get access.

A pack is built only from open data. It is an aid for a desk study, and it does not replace a site inspection, title search, service location or professional assessment.

## What a pack draws on

| Question | In the mirror | Still to source |
|---|---|---|
| Ground surface | 2 m LiDAR DEM, contours, survey control | |
| Geology | | MRT 1:25,000 geology, MRT boreholes |
| Soils | soil mapping, sample sites, acid sulfate soil layers | |
| Groundwater | bore locations and summary fields | NRE driller logs and water levels |
| Flooding | hydrography, flood models, historic flood extents | |
| Ground movement | landslide planning bands | MRT landslide inventory |
| Contamination | EPA regulated sites, aerial photo index | fuel tank and dangerous-goods registers |
| Buried services | water, sewer, power and gas corridor layers, easements | Before You Dig request |
| Planning | zones and code overlays | |
